FOUND-001.title: Conduct Foundation Event Storm for Foundation
FOUND-001.description:
Complete the foundation by capturing domain architecture through Foundation Event Storm.

Use these commands to populate foundation.json eventStorm field:
- fspec add-foundation-bounded-context <name>
- fspec remove-foundation-bounded-context <name> [--cascade]
- fspec add-aggregate-to-foundation <context> <aggregate>
- fspec remove-aggregate-from-foundation <context> <aggregate>
- fspec add-domain-event-to-foundation <context> <event>
- fspec remove-domain-event-from-foundation <context> <event>
- fspec add-command-to-foundation <context> <command>
- fspec remove-command-from-foundation <context> <command>
- fspec show-foundation-event-storm

Why this matters:
- Establishes bounded contexts for domain-driven design
- Enables tag ontology generation from domain model
- Provides foundation for architectural documentation
- Supports EXMAP-004 tag discovery workflow

See spec/AGENTS.md "Foundation Event Storm" section for detailed guidance.

PORT-035.title: Protect contact form with Cloudflare Turnstile
PORT-035.description: Require a valid Cloudflare Turnstile token before the portfolio contact handler sends email, while retaining the current honeypot and graceful user messaging.

userStory.action: complete a bot check before sending a contact message
userStory.benefit: automated spam is less likely to reach Brandon's inbox

rules.text: The contact endpoint must require a non-empty Turnstile response and validate it with Cloudflare Siteverify before requesting Gmail delivery; verification fails closed if configuration is missing or invalid.
The current honeypot remains active, and the public form explains verification or delivery errors without exposing secrets or provider details.

examples.text: A visitor completes the Turnstile check and valid contact fields; the server verifies the token for the expected hostname, then sends the message through Gmail.
A missing, invalid, expired, or wrong-host token is rejected before Google OAuth or Gmail is called; a honeypot submission still receives the generic success response without delivery.
A visitor submits a valid contact message after completing the bot check and sees a confirmation when the message is accepted.
A visitor who skips or fails the bot check is asked to retry; a bot that completes the hidden decoy field sees a generic confirmation, but no email is sent.
A visitor whose bot check expires is asked to complete it again, and the contact message is not delivered.

architectureNotes.text: The contact page receives the public Turnstile site key at static build time. The Pages Function reads the encrypted secret from its runtime environment and calls Cloudflare Siteverify before any OAuth or Gmail request; hostname validation binds the assertion to the incoming request host. Unit tests mock Siteverify and assert missing, rejected, or host-mismatched assertions prevent downstream provider calls.

PORT-036.title: Resume top-level expand/collapse control
PORT-036.description: The online resume's Expand all control does not reliably affect all detail sections and is positioned below the resume heading. Put the control at the top level of the resume and ensure one action opens or closes all expandable sections.

userStory.action: expand or collapse all resume details from a control at the top
userStory.benefit: see the full experience without scrolling to find the control

rules.text: The expand and collapse controls appear at the top of the resume content, before the identity header and all sections.
Expand all opens every expandable detail section, including later sections below the initial viewport; Collapse all closes them all.

examples.text: At page load, all detail disclosures are collapsed. Selecting Expand all opens every disclosure across roles and skills; selecting Collapse all closes every disclosure.
